title: Brachial plexus anatomy: roots to terminal nerves
description: Trace the arm nerve network from spinal roots through trunks, divisions and cords to five terminal nerves.

questions.question: Which spinal nerves form the brachial plexus?
questions.answer: Its main roots usually arise from ventral rami C5 through T1. They organize into trunks, divisions, cords and terminal branches.

questions.question: What are the five major terminal branches of the brachial plexus?
questions.answer: Musculocutaneous, axillary, radial, median and ulnar nerves are the five commonly taught terminal branches.

questions.question: What is the C5–T1 ventral rami?
questions.answer: Five spinal nerve ventral rami build the typical plexus; not the intrathecal dorsal/ventral rootlets. Function: Provide segmental motor and sensory fibers to upper limb.

questions.question: Where is the upper trunk located?
questions.answer: Formed by union of C5 and C6 ventral rami. Function: Redistributes upper-root fibers into divisions.

questions.question: What is the function of the lower trunk?
questions.answer: Function: Carries lower-root fibers toward hand pathways. Formed by C8 and T1 ventral rami.
